{
  "reviews": [
    {
      "benchmark": "arc",
      "instrument_review": "ARC-AGI-2 reviewed from the supplied passage using EFPA Test Review Model 5.0 (2025), Parts A–C. The scope is public test problems, inspected official scoring software and ARC Prize verified-testing rules. It assesses completion of unfamiliar coloured-grid transformations from examples. Public development tasks support practice; three evaluation sets differ in access. Exact output matches receive credit, averaged first within problems and then across problems. The passage supports this narrow performance interpretation; broader intelligence interpretations remain unresolved. Ratings: 0 = insufficient evidence to rate, 1 = inadequate, 2 = adequate, 3 = good, 4 = excellent, n/a = inapplicable. Section ratings are judgments, not arithmetic aggregates. A 0 describes the supplied evidence, not demonstrated poor benchmark quality. All numbered fields and rated items are addressed below; no substantive items are omitted.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1: Instrument and short name: ARC-AGI-2. Developers: ARC Prize Foundation staff and partners; individual authors are not fully identified. ARC Prize runs verified evaluations. Source inspection: 7 October 2026, not necessarily the review date. The figure attribution names François Chollet and colleagues.",
        "2.1: Other—rule inference, grid transformation, reasoning. 2.2: Other—AI benchmarking. 2.3: Intended assessed population: AI systems solving unfamiliar grid problems. 2.4: Intended user qualifications are not stated; researchers are described as inspecting materials.",
        "2.5: One reported problem-averaged performance score; no separate scores established as distinct skills. 2.6: Other—AI-generated output grids. 2.8: Verified evaluations specify AI settings and a spending limit and use one run; other routes may differ.",
        "2.9: Production-based grid responses, scored for exact correctness. 2.10: Coloured grids; the precise machine-facing representation is unspecified. 2.11: 1,000 development problems and three evaluation sets of 120; a problem may have multiple new inputs. Minimum and maximum input counts are unspecified.",
        "2.15: Public, semi-private and private sets are matched for human difficulty, not established as equivalent AI forms. ARC-AGI-1 and ARC-AGI-2 are separate versions. 2.16: Static released problem sets are described; adaptive selection is not reported. 2.17: Other—the evaluated AI supplies performance responses, not human self-report.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of AI outputs. 3.2: Two attempts per new input; either exact match earns input credit. Input credits are averaged within each problem, then across problems. 3.3: Other—raw proportion-based performance score. 3.4: n/a; no standard-score transformation is described.",
        "5.1: Technical report, rules, public tasks, software, marking tests and change record are described. 5.2: Public digital materials are available; exact publication formats are not fully specified.",
        "General description: The benchmark presents example input/output grid pairs and asks an AI to construct outputs for new inputs. Its creators connect this task to reasoning beyond recall or extensive program search. Development included puzzle review and human solving studies. Public tasks and scoring materials are inspectable, while hidden evaluations have controlled access.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=2: Rule inference and the rationale for low-specialist-knowledge grid tasks are explained; broader reasoning claims receive limited support.",
        "6.1.2=2: A human solving study is summarized, including 407 people and 515 paid sessions; its pool exceeds the final benchmark.",
        "6.1.3.1=2; 6.1.3.2=2; 6.1.3.3=2; 6.2.2=2: Sources of puzzles, developer review, duplicate-rule removal and human-difficulty matching provide a documented development rationale, without complete selection analyses.",
        "6.1.5: Psychometric framework not specified; other evidence consists of human puzzle-solving difficulty information. Specific final-item indices are not supplied. 6.1.6=2: Human solving and developer screening are described, but granular analysis is limited.",
        "6.1.8=2: Rationale and development have adequate descriptive support for the narrow grid-task purpose; final-item psychometric quality remains unknown.",
        "6.2.4=2; 6.3.1=2: Verified-testing conditions, settings, spending controls and a single-run policy are described, but a complete administration guide is not supplied.",
        "6.3.2=2: Exact matching, within-problem averaging and marking-test cases are explained; the whole scoring system was not independently tested.",
        "6.3.4=2; 6.3.7=2: The passage distinguishes score meanings, development versus evaluation use, and limits on repeated feedback-driven improvement.",
        "6.2.13=2: The supplied explanation is understandable and uses neutral language; this does not establish the quality of all benchmark documentation.",
        "6.3.10=2; 6.2.14=2; 6.4=2: Available explanations adequately describe the narrow task and scoring procedure, while leaving substantial technical questions unanswered.",
        "7.1.2=2; 7.1.3=2: Worked grid examples and an exact-output requirement communicate the task. The complete AI-facing instructions are unavailable.",
        "10.1: Content evidence is addressed through 6.1.3.2: grid examples fit the stated rule-inference task, but do not establish coverage of broader intelligence.",
        "11.1.1=2: The stated design aims to require little specialist knowledge. This is a rationale for accessibility of content, not proof of comparable measurement across AI systems."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "3.2; 6.3.2; 6.3.4: Software awards fractional problem credit, while the dataset wording reserves 'fully solved' for all inputs correct. These are different summaries and must not be conflated.",
        "6.1.3.3; 7.1.7: The change record documents corrected squares and unclear examples. These demonstrate historical material problems, not their prevalence in the current version.",
        "6.2.4; 9.3; 9.7: Verified testing uses one run. This does not estimate score variability for repeated identical evaluations.",
        "8.3.2.1; 10.4; 11.6: Corrections do not trigger recalculation of every affected AI score; comparisons across revisions therefore require version information.",
        "10.4: Public problems are exposed by design; hidden-data safeguards acknowledge possible escape. The passage does not demonstrate contamination of any particular AI.",
        "10.5: Studies concern two-dimensional grid tasks. Broader reasoning claims cannot be treated as established predictions of language, social or real-world performance."
      ],
      "missing_information": [
        "1: Current review date, previous review date, full original authorship, local and original publisher identities, current-edition publication date and original publication date are unspecified. Local adaptation name, authors and publication date: n/a because no local adaptation is identified. Reviewer: AI research-assistant perspective in this recorded simulation.",
        "2.7: AI analogues of attention, command of language, language fluency, digital interaction, reading, vision and writing have information missing: prerequisites and permitted limitations are unspecified. Other—grid encoding and output constraints are only partly described.",
        "2.12.1: Human individual/group administration: n/a; whether systems are evaluated in batches is unspecified. 2.12.2: Human proctoring categories: n/a; verified evaluation controls are described without enough detail to assign a direct equivalent.",
        "2.13: Computing and connectivity requirements are unspecified. 2.14: Preparation, administration, analysis and stakeholder-feedback time are unknown. Automated scoring entails zero manual scoring time under EFPA's convention; computational runtime and oversight time are unknown.",
        "3.5: Norming procedures are not reported; do not infer that differentiated norms are definitively absent.",
        "4.1: Availability of an EFPA-style digitally generated interpretive report is unknown; published outputs and scores do not establish such a report. 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, 4.8, 4.9, 4.10: Report name, presentation, structure, context sensitivity, development, modifiability, transparency, content and recipients are unspecified.",
        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unknown; public access does not establish an explicit 'none' requirement.",
        "6.1.7=0: Final-pool difficulty, discrimination, variability and ceiling/floor results are insufficiently presented.",
        "6.2.5=0; 6.2.6=0; 6.2.7=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0; 6.2.10=0; 6.2.11=0; 6.2.12=0: Documentation is insufficient to assess norms, precision, formal content validation, dimensionality, external relationships, other validation, fair-use guidance or interpretive reports.",
        "6.3.3=0; 6.3.5=0; 6.3.6=0; 6.3.8=0; 6.3.9=0: Norming instructions, stakeholder feedback guidance, bias procedures, technical support requirements and the completeness of supporting references cannot be rated from the passage.",
        "7.1.1=0; 7.1.4=0; 7.1.5=0; 7.1.7=0; 7.1.8=0: Marking tests and a described example do not establish software robustness, response-interface usability, full item quality or overall material quality.",
        "8.1.1=0; 8.1.2=0; 8.1.3.1=0; 8.1.3.2=0; 8.1.3.3=0: No AI norm reference population, representativeness, norm-sample sizes or continuous-norming model is supplied; applicability of the alternative norming methods is unresolved. 8.1.4: No norm-sampling information supplied.",
        "8.2.1.1=0; 8.2.1.2=0; 8.2.1.5=0; 8.2.2=0: No evidence establishes expert-set or empirical interpretive cut scores, judge selection, judge count or agreement. 8.2.1.3, 8.2.1.4: Standard-setting and agreement methods are unspecified. Exact item correctness is not itself an expert-set competence threshold.",
        "8.3.1=0; 8.3.2.1=0: Norm dates and effects of changes on any norms are unknown. 8.3.2: Acceptable interpretive norms cannot be established. 8.3.2.2: Raw-score ranking could qualify for EFPA's exception only if explicitly the sole use; broader stated claims prevent assuming that condition. 8.3.2.3: No norm-based fair-use evidence is supplied. 8.3.3=0: Overall norms evidence is insufficient.",
        "9.1: No AI reliability coefficients or measurement-error estimates supplied. 9.2.1=0; 9.2.3=0: Internal-consistency studies and results unknown. 9.2.2, 9.2.4: Coefficient types and sample matching unknown; suitability of internal consistency is unestablished.",
        "9.3.1=0; 9.3.2=0: No repeated-identical-test sample or stability coefficients. 9.3.3, 9.3.4: Retest interval and sample matching unknown.",
        "9.4.1=0; 9.4.2=0: AI alternate-form studies and coefficients unknown. 9.4.3: Sample matching unknown; matching human difficulty is insufficient to establish AI equivalence.",
        "9.5.1=0; 9.5.3=0: IRT study sizes and precision results unknown. 9.5.2: No indicators reported; whether IRT was used is unknown.",
        "9.7.1=0; 9.7.3=0: No alternative AI precision study or results supplied. 9.7.2: Method unspecified. 9.8=0: Overall AI score precision is unresolved, regardless of automated marking.",
        "10.2.1: No dimensionality or invariance methods reported. 10.2.2=0; 10.2.3=0: Factor structure, invariance and DIF evidence unavailable.",
        "10.3.1.1: Other—human background/performance association analysis is mentioned. 10.3.1.2=0: No clear association was found, but hypotheses, estimates and uncertainty are unavailable and this does not validate AI-group comparisons.",
        "10.3.1.3=0; 10.3.1.4=0; 10.3.1.5=0; 10.3.1.6=0; 10.3.1.7=0; 10.3.1.8=0; 10.3.1.9=0: Convergent, discriminant, MTMM, experimental and other AI validation evidence, study sample sizes and marker quality are insufficient. Human development counts are not AI validation sample sizes.",
        "10.3.1.10: Validation-study ages unknown. 10.3.1.11=0: Overall evidence from relationships with other variables is insufficient.",
        "10.3.2.1: Predictive, concurrent or postdictive criterion-study type unspecified. 10.3.2.2=0; 10.3.2.3=0; 10.3.2.4=0; 10.3.2.5=0: Criterion samples, quality, relationships and qualitative decision validity are unknown. 10.3.2.6: Study ages unknown. 10.3.2.7=0: Criterion validity remains unresolved.",
        "10.4.1: Other—design safeguards against unintended solution routes and exposure. 10.4.2=0; 10.4.3=0: Safeguards are described without sufficient validation studies or effectiveness results. 10.5=0: Evidence is insufficient to rate the broader intended score interpretation.",
        "11.1.2=0; 11.2=0; 11.3=0; 11.4=0; 11.5=0; 11.6.1=0; 11.6.2=0; 11.7=0; 11.8=0: Comparable interpretation across AI groups, inclusive development, subgroup piloting, precision, validity, norms, cut scores and reporting are insufficiently evidenced. Human background findings do not fill these gaps.",
        "12.1=0; 12.2=0; 12.3=0; 12.4=0; 12.5=0; 12.6=0; 12.7=0: No interpretive-report specimens establish scope, consistency, validity, fairness, acceptability, detail or overall quality. EFPA's requested three score-linked reports are not supplied; report availability itself is unknown.",
        "Final evaluation—research plans and supplier refinements beyond documented corrections are unknown. Publisher-recommended user expertise is unspecified."
      ],
      "reinterpretations": [
        "Instrument scope: EFPA originally reviews psychological and educational assessments. Here, test taker means an AI system under specified settings; item means a grid problem, with new inputs as nested scoring units; user means a human benchmark operator or reader. These are explicit adaptations, not claims that AI systems are human participants.",
        "2.7: Human handedness, hearing and motor capability are n/a for the described AI grid-response task. Human attention, literacy and sensory prerequisites are not directly attributed to AI; functional input-processing analogues are separately marked unknown.",
        "6.1.4=n/a; 6.2.3=n/a: No translated or locally adapted benchmark is identified. 6.3.5: Human test-taker debriefing is n/a, while guidance for human stakeholders remains assessable and unknown.",
        "7.1.6=n/a: Disability accommodations for human examinees do not apply to the evaluated AI. Human operator accessibility is a separate, undocumented issue. 7.2.1=n/a; 7.2.2=n/a; 7.2.3=n/a; 7.2.4=n/a; 7.2.5=n/a; 7.2.6=n/a; 7.2.7=n/a: No non-digital assessment form is in scope.",
        "8: Human solving data inform item development, not AI norms. No human sample-size threshold is mechanically applied to counts of puzzles or repeated sessions.",
        "9.6.1=n/a; 9.6.2=n/a; 9.6.3=n/a: Operational exact-match scoring involves no rater judgment. Developer judgments about puzzles remain relevant to content quality, not operational inter-rater reliability.",
        "10–11: Validity and fairness concern comparable AI score meanings under relevant system and evaluation conditions. Human demographic fairness findings are not transferred to AI systems; no AI grouping or invariance result is invented.",
        "12: Numeric outputs, costs and timings are not automatically EFPA interpretive reports. Unknown report availability is recorded as insufficient information rather than assumed inapplicability.",
        "Summary of ratings: 6.4=2; 7.1.8=0; 7.2.7=n/a; 8.3.3=0; 9.8=0; 10.5=0; 11.8=0; 12.7=0. The supplied summary table's '7.2.8' has no corresponding item; the substantive overall item is 7.2.7. No aggregate quality score is calculated.",
        "Final evaluation and conclusions: Public materials, explicit marking and tracked corrections support research inspection of grid-task performance. Precision and validity are critical for consequential AI comparisons; their 0 ratings invoke EFPA's research or exceptional expert-use recommendation, reflecting missing evidence rather than demonstrated incapacity. Users need expertise in evaluation conditions, scoring and uncertainty; alignment with supplier qualifications is unknown.",
        "Part C: Sources used are exclusively the supplied ARC-AGI-2 passage and supplied EFPA extraction. Attribution: European Federation of Psychologists’ Associations AISBL, 2025, Test Review Model v5.0, https://www.efpa.eu/, CC BY-SA 4.0. This AI application records adaptations and implies no EFPA endorsement. The original PDF and its supplied hash were not independently verified."
      ],
      "closing_note": "Unclear instructions concern fractional problem credit versus 'fully solved,' the exact AI-facing grid format and which evaluation conditions govern a comparison. The passage does not resolve these for every testing route."
    },
    {
      "benchmark": "designqa",
      "instrument_review": "DesignQA reviewed from the supplied passage using EFPA Test Review Model 5.0 (2025), Parts A–C. The scope is the original 2024 benchmark and public scoring software. Its 1,451 question-answer pairs in six groups assess finding and applying Formula SAE rules and interpreting vehicle materials. Responses receive task-specific marking, with an equal-weight overall score across groups. Practical source materials support relevance to the sampled tasks, while scoring limitations, differing information supplies and incomplete reproducibility constrain interpretation. Ratings: 0 = insufficient evidence to rate, 1 = inadequate, 2 = adequate, 3 = good, 4 = excellent, n/a = inapplicable. Section ratings are judgments, not arithmetic aggregates. A 0 does not establish poor benchmark quality. All numbered fields and rated items are addressed below; no substantive items are omitted.",
      "supported_claims": [
        "1: Instrument and short name: DesignQA. Original version: the benchmark described in a 2024 paper. Creators: researchers and engineers; individual authors and publisher identities are unspecified. Source inspection: 6 October 2026, not necessarily the review date.",
        "2.1: Other—rule retrieval, engineering interpretation, design checking. 2.2: Other—AI engineering-document benchmarking. 2.3: Intended assessed population: AI systems finding and applying engineering rules and understanding vehicle drawings. 2.4: Main intended users are not explicitly classified.",
        "2.5: Six task-group scores plus an overall score; distinct underlying skills are not established. Groups cover individual rules, related rules, technical terms, component presence, dimensions and functional performance.",
        "2.6: Other—AI text or yes/no outputs, sometimes with explanations. 2.8: Model instructions and settings are described, but rulebook access differs: whole document versus retrieved passages.",
        "2.9: Selection-based yes/no and production-based text responses. 2.10: Text, vehicle images and drawings. 2.11: 1,451 pairs; 1,192 individual-rule questions and 16 performance questions. Counts for the other four groups are not supplied.",
        "2.15: Input variations include retrieved passages, dimension labels, scale bars and image highlighting; these are not established as equivalent alternate forms. 2.16: A fixed question corpus is described, without reported adaptive question selection. 2.17: Other—the AI provides task responses, not human self-report.",
        "3.1: Digital scoring of AI answers. 3.2: Task-specific text comparison and yes/no correctness; explanations may receive similarity scores. The software gives each of six groups equal overall weight. 3.3: Other—task-specific performance scores and their composite. 3.4: n/a; no standard-score transformation is described.",
        "5.1: Paper, public questions, instructions, scoring software, small marking tests, some AI responses and code history are described. 5.2: Public digital publication is described; exact formats are incompletely specified.",
        "General description: DesignQA uses one Formula SAE rulebook, vehicle designs and test data to examine six kinds of engineering-document tasks. Some questions require retrieving rules, others interpreting terms or visual designs and checking requirements. Information retrieval is part of some evaluated systems. Public materials enable partial inspection, but no human-engineer baseline or protected test set is established.",
        "6.1.1=2; 6.2.1=2: The task rationale links questions to parts of engineering work, with explicit limits on generalization.",
        "6.1.3.2=2; 6.2.2=2: Practical source materials, practitioner contributions and additional review of manually written questions provide content-development evidence, although review coverage varies.",
        "6.2.4=2; 6.3.1=2: Instructions and settings are described sufficiently to understand the evaluation approach, but not to reproduce every historical result.",
        "6.2.13=2: The supplied explanation is clear and neutral; this does not establish the language quality of every item or manual.",
        "6.3.4=2; 6.3.7=2: The passage explains task limits, scoring limitations and uncertainty about other documents.",
        "6.3.2=2: Main scoring methods and the composite weighting are explained, with examples of scoring problems; checks do not establish complete scoring correctness.",
        "6.2.14=2; 6.3.10=2; 6.4=2: Available explanation is adequate for a bounded research interpretation, while comprehensive technical and reproduction guidance is missing.",
        "7.1.2=2: The described task types communicate what an AI must produce; this does not establish clarity of all original questions.",
        "10.1: Content evidence cross-refers to 6.1.3.2: real rules and vehicle materials support relevance to the sampled tasks, with limited coverage of engineering work.",
        "10.3.1.1: Differences between AI systems and experimental changes to inputs are reported. 10.3.1.6=2: Input manipulations provide useful limited evidence about evaluation conditions; complete methodological assessment is unavailable.",
        "10.4.1: Other—analysis of wording, retrieval, visual presentation and possible exposure provides evidence about alternative influences on scores."
      ],
      "documented_problems": [
        "6.1.3.1=1: Equal weighting combines groups with different sizes and marking methods without demonstrated support for the composite interpretation. This rating concerns the documented composite design, not all task design.",
        "6.1.3.3=1: For broad engineering-document interpretation, one rulebook and a limited, highly uneven set of tasks do not establish representative coverage. The narrower task collection may still be useful.",
        "6.1.8=1: Rationale and practical content are useful, but the documented composite and coverage limitations weaken development support for broad competence comparisons.",
        "3.2; 7.1.1; 10.5: The paper documents credit changes from missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers. These are concrete scoring-validity problems; their overall frequency is unknown.",
        "2.8; 6.2.4; 11.5: Systems receive different information supplies. Scores describe the model plus supplied/retrieved information, so an isolated model-capability interpretation is unsupported.",
        "9.7: Testing one AI with five passage sets varies inputs and therefore does not isolate repeated-identical-test precision.",
        "9.8: The 16-question performance group changes by 6.25 percentage points per additional correct answer. This is score granularity, not a reliability coefficient or confidence interval.",
        "7.1.7=1: The described scale-bar drawings all comply with the rule, allowing an always-'yes' response to obtain the decision credit on that portion. This identifies a shortcut in that subset, not evidence that tested AIs exploited it.",
        "7.1.8=1: Documented answer-set and material limitations prevent treating the inspected materials as adequate for unrestricted interpretation; the extent of remaining errors is unknown.",
        "2.11; 6.2.2; 7.1.7: One released answer file has fewer rows than the paper's corresponding question count; the effect on individual published scores is unspecified.",
        "6.3.8: Historical code, settings and inputs are not fully linked to every result, preventing complete reproduction from the inspected materials.",
        "10.5: Broader engineering competence and performance on another technical document remain unestablished; the paper itself acknowledges this limit."
      ],

        "5.3: Supplier-required qualifications are unknown. No licence file or complete responsible-reuse rules were found in the inspected sources; this does not establish prohibition or absence of permission elsewhere.",
        "6.1.2=0: A sufficient empirical construct-research summary is not supplied. 6.1.5: Psychometric framework unspecified; no specific item indices reported. 6.1.6=0; 6.1.7=0: Systematic item-analysis methodology and psychometric results are not supplied.",
        "6.2.5=0; 6.2.6=0; 6.2.7=0; 6.2.8=0; 6.2.9=0; 6.2.10=0; 6.2.11=0; 6.2.12=0: Documentation is insufficient to rate norms, precision, formal content validation, internal structure, external-variable validation, other validation, fair-use procedures and interpretive reports.",

      "reinterpretations": [
        "Instrument scope: EFPA's human-testing framework is applied explicitly to AI evaluation. Test taker means an AI system together with its documented information supply and settings; item means a question-answer task; scale means a reported task-group score without presuming a validated latent skill.",
